newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler offers $1,000 incentive on minivans.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler offers $1,000 incentive on minivans.

text.p: Chrysler Corp, acknowledging stiffer competition in the U.S. minivan market, said Wednesday it is raising cash incentives on its minivans to up to $1,000 from $595.

Chrysler said the new program, which runs through July 7, offers $750 allowances to retail customers who buy or lease new, short-base 1996 or 1997 Dodge Caravan, Plymouth Voyager and Chrysler Town & Country models.
The automaker is offering $1,000 rebates to customers who buy or lease 1996 or 1997 long-wheelbase versions of its minivans.

Chrysler said the new incentives replace a program that expired Tuesday that offered free sliding driver-side rear doors to minivan buyers at a cost of $595. Although the new program offers a higher cash value, the fourth door is once again an extra-cost option.

Chrysler's minivan sales for the first four months of 1997 were down four percent from a year earlier to 168,982 vans. General Motors Corp is in the process of launching an all-new trio of minivans, that have increased competition at a time when overall sales in the minivan segment are declining.
Minivan sales this year through April have fallen 3.1 percent to 395,154, according to J.D. Power and Associates.

Chrysler still dominates the sector and James Holden, the company's executive vice president of sales, service and marketing said the incentives are aimed at holding on to Chrysler's nearly 43 percent share of the market.
"This sales will allow consumers to buy the best for even less and keep Chrysler, Plymouth and Dodge minivans at the top of the segment," Holden said in a statement.
